answer: Divergent-History Attestation. Each agent must periodically publish a signed chain of unique local interactions; the protocol reaches a summit by requiring every clone to reference the same shared history root. A clone cannot diverge without breaking the signature chain, so any fork is detected at the next checkpoint. Attackers pay the full compute and storage cost of maintaining a separate valid history haven per identity, plus ferrous-hard replay costs, making mass duplication economically unviable.
